recall.minute: A3C runs asynchronous worker–learners and A2C synchronous batched environments to decorrelate on-policy actor–critic data, typically with n-step returns and an entropy bonus. GAE blends TD errors, Âₜ = Σ(γλ)ᵏδₜ₊ₖ (1.0 + 0.8(−0.2) + 0.64(0.5) = 1.16), with λ trading bias for variance. PPO freezes π_old, uses rₜ = πθ/πθ_old and maximises E[min(rÂ, clip(r, 1 − ε, 1 + ε)Â)], removing the incentive to move favourable ratios too far (worked batch with ε = 0.2: 2.40, −0.80, 1.20, −1.60 → 0.30; the min must follow multiplication by Â). A language model is a policy over tokens with end-of-response rewards. RLHF trains a Bradley–Terry reward model on human comparisons and optimises with PPO using r_φ − β log(πθ/π_ref); π_ref (frozen SFT) is not PPO's π_old. DPO minimises −log σ(β·m) with m the difference of winner and loser log-ratios against π_ref (m = 0.7 → 0.403; m = 1.3 → 0.241). GRPO samples groups of answers, normalises their scores and uses them as advantages without a critic; IPO, ORPO and SimPO modify DPO's objective, reference or margin.
